title: Roos and intrinsic completeness for completed local-field coefficients
statement: Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation ring $A$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=A/(t^n)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Assume $(A,(t))$ satisfies [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For a scheme $T$ use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $R=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Form the strict reductions on one flat-term K-flat representative [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Let $\operatorname{comp}_K:K\to R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n K_n$ be the canonical quotient augmentation, let $\kappa_K$ be the functorial Koszul unit of [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], and let $\eta_K$ be the explicit product-fibre unit of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Then the following are equivalent: (i) $K$ satisfies the Roos-triangle convention of [def-weil-derived-complete]; (ii) $K$ is locally derived $t$-complete, meaning that on every slice and for every local section $b$ of $tR$, $R\mathcal Hom(R_U[1/b],K|_U)=0$, where $U$ is the slice object and $R_U[1/b]$ is the sheafified sectionwise localization placed in degree zero [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; (iii) $\kappa_K$ is invertible; (iv) $\eta_K$ is invertible; (v) $\operatorname{comp}_K$ is invertible. The units in (iii)--(v) are the specified canonical units, not arbitrary isomorphisms to a limit object.

proof.text: Use the independent-universe principal-cone local criterion at the actual uniformizer section. Naturality of the constant-to-completion map supplies the natural section hypothesis. The scalar endomorphism is characterized by its sectionwise formula. This proves (ii) iff (iii), and local completeness of the scalar-cone completion. The concrete scalar-cone compatibility declarations apply the generic PrincipalCone square, compatible and productUnit_comp identities.

Apply the normalized principal-cone/finite-quotient comparison on the K-flat representative P. It preserves the whole zero-homotopy unit. Naturality of the canonical quotient completion unit and its normalization on good representatives identify e inverse followed by this strict quotient unit with the completion unit at K followed by isomorphisms. Cancellation gives (iii) iff (v).

The squares (1,-1) give mutually inverse chain maps between Cone(-(1-shift)) and Cone(1-shift). Shift by -1. The cone-map formulas show that this isomorphism carries the lift with product component u and zero homotopy to the corresponding lift. Therefore (iii) iff (iv).

Exact countable products make localization preserve the countable product of complexes. Map the distinguished mapping-cocone triangle to the derived category and use the product comparison to get the normalized strict Roos triangle, whose first components are precisely the localized cocone projection followed by each product projection.

Assuming (i), choose its K-flat resolution representative and triangle. The operations quotient-tower transitions agree with the canonical reduction transitions by their sectionwise normalization. Rotate its triangle and the normalized strict Roos triangle so both first arrows are 1-shift. Complete the two identity isomorphisms to a triangle isomorphism, and shift back to identify K with the strict quotient Roos object. The principal-cone comparison and local criterion make that object locally complete; exact slice restriction and functorial RHom transfer vanishing along the isomorphism. This gives (ii) without identifying an arbitrary TR3 lift with the specified unit.

Assuming (v), the normalized strict quotient unit from K is invertible by naturality and its representative comparison. Transport the strict Roos triangle along that precise isomorphism. Its product components are the canonical quotient augmentation, by the zero-homotopy lift formula. With identity resolution of the given K-flat P and the auxiliary finite-field datum of characteristic p this is exactly the global Roos completeness witness (i). The TFAE implications now give all five equivalences.

Step 1: the reflector lemma with O=R and the section t has ideal tR, so its local condition is exactly (ii); it gives (ii)<=>(iii) and local completeness of the completion. OK. Steps 4-6 are correct: the strict augmentation (0,(gamma_n)) composed with iota equals c; steps 5 and 6 use the def's Equivalently clause, rotation, TR3 on (id,id) and two-of-three, and do not claim the TR3 map is comp_K. Fault 1 (E4/C4), step 2: it applied prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction, which is stated over the datum ring A_T (continuous-function sheaf), to K in D(Mod R) with R the constant-sheaf ring of def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients. This silently identifies two coefficient rings the DAG keeps apart. Fix: transport through e_{E,T} and Phi_{E,T} of def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport (same unit); restriction along the ring isomorphism matches the Koszul complexes, strict quotient towers and the units kappa, comp, eta. Fault 2 (C4/E5), step 3: lem-weil-pbc-completed-fiber-strict-limit-comparison gives D.unit(F(QC)) for a presentation D on the lifted AsSmall site with the pulled-back ring, not F(kappa_K); the claim 'choose D to be the same tower used for Lambda' is unavailable. The equivalences still close: (ii)<=>(iii), (iii)<=>(v), (iv)<=>(v), (v)=>(i), (i)=>(ii). I updated proof_deps and split_report.tool_uses (removed the strict-limit comparison, added the quotient comparison); every step is under 2000 characters.
